2026 · Monetisation

AI Credits Wallet

One shared credits wallet for free and premium users, across Wix and Wixel.

TL;DR

The problemI designed one credits wallet for free and premium users, and it now runs in the Business Manager, Wixel, Wixel mobile and several verticals.

ProcessI mapped the billing model with Premium, the verticals and Legal, led the content, and fixed bugs in code.

The resultCredit use rose gradually after launch.

The problemExplaining a new AI credits model

Some of Wix's AI features started to consume credits, with two tiers: free users and subscribers, and across the Wix Business Manager, Wixel and Wixel mobile.

The real problem was helping users understand a new billing model.

What users needed to understand

How many credits are left?

Free plans and premium plans

When do credits reset?

How to top-up or upgrade?

Site plans, one account-wide wallet

ApproachMapping the credits model with each team

I discussed what they needed with each team, and researched competitors.

The wallet had to stay platformic: the same in all products.

Where the input came from

Premium team. What the two tiers are.

AI verticals. Some wanted their own balance widget with a progress bar. We needed one consistent platform solution, so the widget is also embeddable.

Legal team. What we can say about credits and billing.

Wixel team. They already had a wallet. We kept most of it and changed parts so it works the same across all products.

Competitors. How other AI products show credits.

Design principles

We decided on four rules.

01

One wallet everywhere

Wix and Wixel share the same balance, logic and component in code, across two design systems.

Consistency
02

Legal shapes the wording

Credits are money, so Legal had a big say in what we must show and how we word it.

Compliance
03

Warn early

Notifications come before users are blocked, to drive upgrades.

Monetization
04

Keep it minimal

The widget had to be small, showing only what users need: balance, renewal date and next step.

Simplicity

SolutionOne wallet skeleton, two tiers, three platforms

  1. Two tiers: Free users see a daily balance with a monthly cap. Premium users see a monthly balance and a renewal date.
  2. One component: A shared skeleton for both design systems, Wix Backoffice and Wixel desktop and mobile.
  3. Two modes: A standalone widget, or embedded in a page for some verticals.
  4. Upgrade: An upgrade button sits next to the widget in all active states.
  5. All the states: Low credits, out of credits, loading, error and no permission, with a notification and a paywall modal.

Where users see their credits

  • Business Manager. In the top bar.
  • Wixel and Wixel mobile. In the top bars.
  • Embedded. Some verticals also show the component inside a page, where it's relevant, so it needed some overrides.

Behind the scenes

Delivery & challengesWorking with the team

Process

Mapped the billing model. For both tiers.

PRD and scoping. I worked on the PRD and the scope with Premium, AI verticals, Wixel and Legal.

Owned the content. Briefed UX writers and approved the final copy.

Did QA, bug and UI fixes. In code.

Challenges

Two mental models. Reconciled in one experience.

One component. Some verticals wanted many design changes to embed it. We met in the middle with variants.

Wixel's model changes. Wixel aligned to the new tiers.

Critical states. Designing where a misunderstanding could disrupt a task.

A lot of opinions on content and design. Legal required the copy, Wixel wanted less. We compromised, and I bridged the gaps.

Impact & next stepsWhat happened after launch

We went from a credits wallet that existed only in Wixel to one shared wallet for free and premium users.

In use

Credit use rose gradually after launch.

Upgrade rate

Upgrade rate improved after we added an upgrade button right where the widget appears.

The shared component

Designers use it in their designs, and verticals with AI features that use credits are expected to use this component.

Next steps

A credits area where managers see usage and distribute credits, a collaborator wallet, and more verticals adopting credits.
